patent_grounding.rationale: The revision-3 components and behavior match the cited claim and description passages: resiliently variable frame elements, resilient inner-surface linkage, actuator force on the second element relative to support, contour response, compliant-surface communication, and coupler/support attachment. The single-frame model's stated scope is explicit; the support spar is identified only as an example. Torque conversion is described as an embodiment rather than imposed as a specific actuator architecture.

functional_completeness.rationale: For the declared claim-1 core scope, FRAME, LINK, ACT, COUPLER, SUPPORT and SURFACE represent the needed mechanism and boundary entities, and CHANGE_CONTOUR traces the supported actuation-to-contour response. Paired-frame variants and alternate embodiments are expressly omitted rather than silently conflated.

flow_consistency.rationale: Revision 3 distinguishes actuator force, resilient linkage coupling, structural attachment, and compliant-surface contour communication with respective flows. Their interface references align to compatible endpoint port types and their stated semantics. The behavior sequence coherently connects actuation, frame deformation, and surface contour response.

claim_traceability.rationale: The modeled mechanism is explicitly identified as the claim-1 arrangement, with the frame coupler supported by claim 2/description. Relevant components, ports, interfaces, item flows, and action have patent citations; claim variants not represented are not presented as part of the model.

interfaces.rationale: Each modeled interface mates existing subsystem ports of compatible flow types, uses existing subsystem IDs, and is recorded once. The coupler links frame to support; the actuator applies force to frame; linkage ends couple to inner-surface ports; the surface receives contour communication. Distinct flow semantics corrected the revision-2 concerns.

textbook_application.rationale: The context/interface guidance supports explicit treatment of a system boundary and external support/surface entities, and functional decomposition guidance is consistent with separating components from verb-noun functions. The torque-to-force textbook retrieval is unrelated regression material; no textbook-derived invention fact or unsupported actuator detail is used.

summary: Independent review of saved SJS 1.0 revision 3: no actionable patent-grounding, functional-completeness, flow, traceability, interface, or structural issues found. The revision resolves the prior interface-flow semantic warnings by separating linkage coupling and structural attachment from actuator force and contour output. Modeling scope and external context are clearly stated and evidence-backed.
